passages.text: Saul was thirty years old when he became king, and he reigned over Israel forty-two years.
passages.sermon: Saul became king of Israel when he was thirty years old.\r\nSaul ruled over Israel for forty-two years.
passages.original: בֶּן־ שָׁנָ֖ה שָׁא֣וּל בְּמָלְכ֑וֹ וּשְׁתֵּ֣י שָׁנִ֔ים מָלַ֖ךְ עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: He chose for himself three thousand men of Israel: Two thousand were with Saul at Michmash and in the hill country of Bethel, and a thousand were with Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin. And the rest of the troops he sent away, each to his own home.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul chose three thousand men from Israel.
Two thousand men stayed with Saul.
They were at Michmash and in the hill country of Bethel.
One thousand men stayed with Jonathan.
Jonathan was at Gibeah in the land of Benjamin.
Saul sent the rest of the people away.
Each man went to his own home.
passages.original: וַיִּבְחַר־ ל֨וֹ שָׁא֜וּל שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת אֲלָפִים֮ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל֒ וַיִּהְי֨וּ עִם־ שָׁא֜וּל אַלְפַּ֗יִם בְּמִכְמָשׂ֙ וּבְהַ֣ר בֵּֽית־ אֵ֔ל וְאֶ֗לֶף הָיוּ֙ עִם־ י֣וֹנָתָ֔ן בְּגִבְעַ֖ת בִּנְיָמִ֑ין וְיֶ֣תֶר הָעָ֔ם שִׁלַּ֖ח אִ֥ישׁ לְאֹהָלָֽיו׃

passages.text: Then Jonathan attacked the Philistine outpost at Geba, and the Philistines heard about it. So Saul blew the ram’s horn throughout the land, saying, “Let the Hebrews hear!”
passages.sermon:
Jonathan was the son of Saul, the king of Israel.
Jonathan attacked the Philistine outpost at Geba.
The Philistines heard about Jonathan’s attack.
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul blew the ram’s horn throughout the land.
Saul said, “Let the Hebrews hear!”
passages.original: וַיַּ֣ךְ יוֹנָתָ֗ן אֵ֣ת נְצִ֤יב פְּלִשְׁתִּים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּגֶ֔בַע וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֖וּ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וְשָׁאוּל֩ תָּקַ֨ע בַּשּׁוֹפָ֤ר בְּכָל־ הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יִשְׁמְע֖וּ הָעִבְרִֽים׃

passages.text: And all Israel heard the news: “Saul has attacked an outpost of the Philistines, and now Israel has become a stench to the Philistines!” Then the people were summoned to join Saul at Gilgal.
passages.sermon:
All the people of Israel heard the news.
They heard that Saul attacked a Philistine outpost.
They also heard that Israel had become hated by the Philistines.
The people gathered and followed Saul at Gilgal.
passages.original: וְכָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֞ל שָׁמְע֣וּ לֵאמֹ֗ר הִכָּ֤ה שָׁאוּל֙ אֶת־ נְצִ֣יב פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וְגַם־ נִבְאַשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בַּפְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיִּצָּעֲק֥וּ הָעָ֛ם אַחֲרֵ֥י שָׁא֖וּל הַגִּלְגָּֽל׃

passages.text: Now the Philistines assembled to fight against Israel with three thousand chariots, six thousand horsemen, and troops as numerous as the sand on the seashore. They went up and camped at Michmash, east of Beth-aven.
passages.sermon:
The Philistines gathered their army.
They wanted to fight Israel.
They brought three thousand chariots.
They brought six thousand horsemen.
They brought many soldiers.
Their soldiers were as many as the sand on the seashore.
The Philistines went up to Michmash.
They set up camp at Michmash.
Michmash is east of Beth-aven.
passages.original: וּפְלִשְׁתִּ֞ים נֶאֶסְפ֣וּ׀ לְהִלָּחֵ֣ם עִם־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל שְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים אֶ֤לֶף רֶ֙כֶב֙ וְשֵׁ֤שֶׁת אֲלָפִים֙ פָּרָשִׁ֔ים וְעָ֕ם כַּח֛וֹל אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־ שְׂפַֽת־ הַיָּ֖ם לָרֹ֑ב וַֽיַּעֲלוּ֙ וַיַּחֲנ֣וּ בְמִכְמָ֔שׂ קִדְמַ֖ת בֵּ֥ית אָֽוֶן׃

passages.text: Seeing that they were in danger because their troops were hard-pressed, the men of Israel hid in caves and thickets, among the rocks, and in cellars and cisterns.
passages.sermon:
The men of Israel saw that they were in danger.
Their enemies pressed them hard.
The men of Israel hid.
They hid in caves.
They hid in thickets.
They hid among the rocks.
They hid in cellars.
They hid in cisterns.
passages.original: וְאִ֨ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל רָאוּ֙ כִּ֣י צַר־ ל֔וֹ כִּ֥י נִגַּ֖שׂ הָעָ֑ם וַיִּֽתְחַבְּא֣וּ הָעָ֗ם בַּמְּעָר֤וֹת וּבַֽחֲוָחִים֙ וּבַסְּלָעִ֔ים וּבַצְּרִחִ֖ים וּבַבֹּרֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Some Hebrews even crossed the Jordan into the land of Gad and Gilead. Saul, however, remained at Gilgal, and all his troops were quaking in fear.
passages.sermon:
Some Hebrews crossed the Jordan River.
They went into the land of Gad and Gilead.
Saul stayed at Gilgal.
All the people with Saul were afraid.
They trembled behind him.
passages.original: וְעִבְרִ֗ים עָֽבְרוּ֙ אֶת־ הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן אֶ֥רֶץ גָּ֖ד וְגִלְעָ֑ד וְשָׁאוּל֙ עוֹדֶ֣נּוּ בַגִּלְגָּ֔ל וְכָל־ הָעָ֖ם חָרְד֥וּ אַחֲרָֽיו׃

passages.text: And Saul waited seven days for the time appointed by Samuel, but Samuel did not come to Gilgal, and the troops began to desert Saul.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul waited seven days.
Samuel had set this time.
Samuel did not come to Gilgal.
The troops began to leave Saul.
passages.original: וַיִּיחֶל שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֗ים לַמּוֹעֵד֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל וְלֹא־ בָ֥א שְׁמוּאֵ֖ל הַגִּלְגָּ֑ל וַיָּ֥פֶץ הָעָ֖ם מֵעָלָֽיו׃

passages.text: So he said, “Bring me the burnt offering and the peace offerings.” And he offered up the burnt offering.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul saw that his troops were afraid.
Saul saw that his troops were leaving him.
Saul was at Gilgal.
Saul spoke to the people near him.
Saul said, “Bring me the burnt offering.”
Saul also said, “Bring me the peace offerings.”
They brought the offerings to Saul.
Saul offered the burnt offering to God.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֔וּל הַגִּ֣שׁוּ אֵלַ֔י הָעֹלָ֖ה וְהַשְּׁלָמִ֑ים וַיַּ֖עַל הָעֹלָֽה׃

passages.text: Just as he finished offering the burnt offering, Samuel arrived, and Saul went out to greet him.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul finished offering the burnt offering.
Samuel arrived at that moment.
Saul went out to greet Samuel.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י כְּכַלֹּתוֹ֙ לְהַעֲל֣וֹת הָעֹלָ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה שְׁמוּאֵ֖ל בָּ֑א וַיֵּצֵ֥א שָׁא֛וּל לִקְרָאת֖וֹ לְבָרֲכֽוֹ׃

passages.text: “What have you done?” Samuel asked. And Saul replied, “When I saw that the troops were deserting me, and that you did not come at the appointed time and the Philistines were gathering at Michmash, I thought, ‘Now the Philistines will descend upon me at Gilgal, and I have not sought the favor of the LORD.’ So I felt compelled to offer the burnt offering.”
passages.sermon:
Samuel was a prophet of the LORD.
Samuel asked Saul a question.
Samuel said, “What have you done?”
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul answered Samuel.
Saul said, “I saw that the people were leaving me.”
Saul said, “You did not come at the appointed time.”
Saul said, “The Philistines were gathering at Michmash.”
Saul said, “I thought the Philistines would come down against me at Gilgal.”
Saul said, “I had not sought the favor of the LORD.”
Saul said, “I felt compelled.”
Saul said, “I offered the burnt offering.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵ֖ל מֶ֣ה עָשִׂ֑יתָ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֡וּל כִּֽי־ רָאִיתִי֩ כִֽי־ נָפַ֨ץ הָעָ֜ם מֵעָלַ֗י וְאַתָּה֙ לֹא־ בָ֙אתָ֙ לְמוֹעֵ֣ד הַיָּמִ֔ים וּפְלִשְׁתִּ֖ים נֶאֱסָפִ֥ים מִכְמָֽשׂ׃ וָאֹמַ֗ר עַ֠תָּה יֵרְד֨וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֤ים אֵלַי֙ הַגִּלְגָּ֔ל וּפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה לֹ֣א חִלִּ֑יתִי וָֽאֶתְאַפַּ֔ק וָאַעֲלֶ֖ה הָעֹלָֽה׃ס

passages.text: “You have acted foolishly,” Samuel declared. “You have not kept the command that the LORD your God gave you; if you had, the LORD would have established your kingdom over Israel for all time.
passages.sermon:
Samuel was a prophet of God.
Saul was the king of Israel.
Samuel spoke to Saul.
Samuel said, “You have acted foolishly.”
Samuel said, “You did not keep the command of the LORD your God.”
The LORD your God gave you this command.
If you had obeyed, the LORD would have established your kingdom over Israel forever.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵ֛ל אֶל־ שָׁא֖וּל נִסְכָּ֑לְתָּ לֹ֣א שָׁמַ֗רְתָּ אֶת־ מִצְוַ֞ת יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֙יךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֔ךְ כִּ֣י עַתָּ֗ה הֵכִ֨ין יְהוָ֧ה אֶת־ מַֽמְלַכְתְּךָ֛ אֶל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַד־ עוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: But now your kingdom will not endure; the LORD has sought a man after His own heart and appointed him ruler over His people, because you have not kept the command of the LORD.”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Samuel spoke to Saul.
Samuel said Saul’s kingdom would not last.
The LORD had looked for a new man.
The LORD wanted a man who loved Him deeply.
The LORD found such a man.
The LORD chose this man to rule His people.
The LORD did this because Saul did not obey His command.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֖ה מַמְלַכְתְּךָ֣ לֹא־ תָק֑וּם בִּקֵּשׁ֩ יְהוָ֨ה ל֜וֹ אִ֣ישׁ כִּלְבָב֗וֹ וַיְצַוֵּ֨הוּ יְהוָ֤ה לְנָגִיד֙ עַל־ עַמּ֔וֹ כִּ֚י לֹ֣א שָׁמַ֔רְתָּ אֵ֥ת אֲשֶֽׁר־ צִוְּךָ֖ יְהוָֽה׃פ

passages.text: Then Samuel set out from Gilgal and went up to Gibeah in Benjamin. And Saul numbered the troops who were with him, about six hundred men.
passages.sermon:
Samuel was a prophet of God.
Samuel stood up.
Samuel left Gilgal.
Samuel went up to Gibeah in the land of Benjamin.
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul counted the people who were with him.
About six hundred men were with Saul.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣קָם שְׁמוּאֵ֗ל וַיַּ֛עַל מִן־ הַגִּלְגָּ֖ל גִּבְעַ֣ת בִּנְיָמִ֑ן וַיִּפְקֹ֣ד שָׁא֗וּל אֶת־ הָעָם֙ הַנִּמְצְאִ֣ים עִמּ֔וֹ כְּשֵׁ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת אִֽישׁ׃

passages.text: Now Saul and Jonathan his son and the troops with them were staying in Geba of Benjamin, while the Philistines camped at Michmash.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Jonathan was Saul’s son.
Some troops stayed with Saul and Jonathan.
They all stayed in Geba.
Geba was in the territory of Benjamin.
The Philistines were Israel’s enemies.
The Philistines set up camp at Michmash.
passages.original: וְשָׁא֞וּל וְיוֹנָתָ֣ן בְּנ֗וֹ וְהָעָם֙ הַנִּמְצָ֣א עִמָּ֔ם יֹשְׁבִ֖ים בְּגֶ֣בַע בִּנְיָמִ֑ן וּפְלִשְׁתִּ֖ים חָנ֥וּ בְמִכְמָֽשׂ׃

passages.text: And raiders went out of the Philistine camp in three divisions. One headed toward Ophrah in the land of Shual, another toward Beth-horon, and the third down the border road overlooking the Valley of Zeboim facing the wilderness.
passages.sermon:
The Philistines were Israel’s enemies.
The Philistines had a camp.
Raiders came out from the Philistine camp.
There were three groups of raiders.
The first group went toward Ophrah.
Ophrah was in the land of Shual.
The second group went toward Beth-horon.
The third group went down the border road.
This road overlooked the Valley of Zeboim.
The Valley of Zeboim faced the wilderness.
passages.original: וַיֵּצֵ֧א הַמַּשְׁחִ֛ית מִמַּחֲנֵ֥ה פְלִשְׁתִּ֖ים שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה רָאשִׁ֑ים הָרֹ֨אשׁ אֶחָ֥ד יִפְנֶ֛ה אֶל־ דֶּ֥רֶךְ עָפְרָ֖ה אֶל־ אֶ֥רֶץ שׁוּעָֽל׃ וְהָרֹ֤אשׁ אֶחָד֙ יִפְנֶ֔ה דֶּ֖רֶךְ בֵּ֣ית חֹר֑וֹן וְהָרֹ֨אשׁ אֶחָ֤ד יִפְנֶה֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַגְּב֔וּל הַנִּשְׁקָ֛ף עַל־ גֵּ֥י הַצְּבֹעִ֖ים הַמִּדְבָּֽרָה׃ס

passages.text: And no blacksmith could be found in all the land of Israel, because the Philistines had said, “The Hebrews must not be allowed to make swords or spears.”
passages.sermon:
The Philistines ruled over Israel at this time.
No blacksmith lived anywhere in the land of Israel.
The Philistines made this rule.
They said, “The Hebrews must not make swords or spears.”
They wanted to keep the Israelites from making weapons.
passages.original: וְחָרָשׁ֙ לֹ֣א יִמָּצֵ֔א בְּכֹ֖ל אֶ֣רֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּֽי־ אָמַר פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים פֶּ֚ן יַעֲשׂ֣וּ הָעִבְרִ֔ים חֶ֖רֶב א֥וֹ חֲנִֽית׃

passages.text: Instead, all the Israelites would go down to the Philistines to sharpen their plowshares, mattocks, axes, and sickles.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites lived in the land of Israel.
The Philistines controlled the land.
No blacksmith lived in Israel.
The Philistines did not allow blacksmiths in Israel.
The Philistines wanted to keep the Israelites weak.
The Philistines did not want the Israelites to make swords or spears.
The Israelites needed to sharpen their tools.
The Israelites had plowshares, mattocks, axes, and sickles.
Each Israelite went down to the Philistines.
Each Israelite brought his plowshare, mattock, axe, or sickle.
The Philistines sharpened the tools for the Israelites.
passages.original: וַיֵּרְד֥וּ כָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים לִ֠לְטוֹשׁ אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־ מַחֲרַשְׁתּ֤וֹ וְאֶת־ אֵתוֹ֙ וְאֶת־ קַרְדֻּמּ֔וֹ וְאֵ֖ת מַחֲרֵשָׁתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: The charge was a pim for sharpening a plowshare or mattock, a third of a shekel for sharpening a pitchfork or an axe, and a third of a shekel for repointing an oxgoad.
passages.sermon:
The Philistines controlled all blacksmithing in Israel.
They set the prices for sharpening tools.
They charged a pim to sharpen a plowshare.
They charged a pim to sharpen a mattock.
They charged a third of a shekel to sharpen a pitchfork.
They charged a third of a shekel to sharpen an axe.
They charged a third of a shekel to repoint an oxgoad.
passages.original: וְֽהָיְתָ֞ה הַפְּצִ֣ירָה פִ֗ים לַמַּֽחֲרֵשֹׁת֙ וְלָ֣אֵתִ֔ים וְלִשְׁלֹ֥שׁ קִלְּשׁ֖וֹן וּלְהַקַּרְדֻּמִּ֑ים וּלְהַצִּ֖יב הַדָּרְבָֽן׃

passages.text: So on the day of battle not a sword or spear could be found in the hands of the troops with Saul and Jonathan; only Saul and his son Jonathan had weapons.
passages.sermon:
On the day of battle, the Israelites fought the Philistines.
Saul was the king of Israel.
Jonathan was Saul’s son.
Saul and Jonathan led the Israelite troops.
None of the Israelite soldiers with Saul and Jonathan had a sword or a spear.
Only Saul had a weapon.
Only Jonathan had a weapon.
No other Israelite soldier had a sword or spear.
passages.original: וְהָיָה֙ בְּי֣וֹם מִלְחֶ֔מֶת וְלֹ֨א נִמְצָ֜א חֶ֤רֶב וַחֲנִית֙ בְּיַ֣ד כָּל־ הָעָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֶת־ שָׁא֖וּל וְאֶת־ יוֹנָתָ֑ן וַתִּמָּצֵ֣א לְשָׁא֔וּל וּלְיוֹנָתָ֖ן בְּנֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And a garrison of the Philistines had gone out to the pass at Michmash.
passages.sermon:
The Philistines were enemies of Israel.
A group of Philistine soldiers left their camp.
They went to the pass at Michmash.
This group was a garrison.
They took positions at the pass.
passages.original: וַיֵּצֵא֙ מַצַּ֣ב פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים אֶֽל־ מַעֲבַ֖ר מִכְמָֽשׂ׃ס
